goals: Provide a lightweight, polished, Minecraft-native personal notebook for Minecraft Java 26.2 Fabric without requiring an item or server component.
Keep canonical user-authored notes pleasant to inspect and edit outside Minecraft as ordinary UTF-8 Markdown files with real authored line breaks.
Support stable multi-note organization, explicit user-controlled ordering, and a deliberately small reading/presentation layer without becoming a general document editor.
scope: Provide a configurable client key mapping, defaulting to N from gameplay, plus one compact collision-aware utility button on survival and creative player inventory screens using current Fabric Screen API lifecycle events and live container bounds.

Present a responsive two-page journal whose left page is a scrollable selectable index with persistent drag-and-drop ordering and whose right page is a vertically scrollable selected note that enters ordinary-text title/body editing directly at a clicked location.

Support create, rename, edit, delete with confirmation, select, scroll, reload, and explicit manual reordering for independently named notes whose stable UUID identity is separate from display title and portable file name.

Render a leading # heading and plain-text checklist markers [ ], [x], and [X] in reading mode; clicking a rendered checkbox changes only the underlying marker while edit mode remains ordinary multiline text.
Store one UTF-8 Markdown file per note under config/notebook/notes, with note-free machine metadata in config/notebook/notebook.json for UUIDs, file associations, selected note, and exact order.

Reconcile files on each Notebook screen open and explicit in-screen reload: retain known identities for known files, reload external body edits, append external valid Markdown files, remove deleted references, treat external renames conservatively as delete-plus-create, and rebuild malformed or stale metadata without guessing content identity.

Use same-directory temporary writes with atomic replacement where supported, debounced dirty-edit autosaves, forced transition saves, and three rotating prior-content Markdown backups per stable note UUID without consuming backup history for each autosave in one edit session.
Keep stable identity and machine-owned metadata extensible for later note-tab shortcuts and one HUD-pinned note without implementing either feature in Canary 1.

exclusions: Physical notebook items, server components, networking, world-save or player-NBT storage, multiplayer collaborative documents, reminders, calendars, quests, folders, databases, images, attachments, or document management.

A broad Markdown implementation, rich-text or WYSIWYG editing, filesystem line breaks derived from GUI wrapping, encoded note bodies, or note content stored inside JSON, NBT, or another machine-oriented container.

Visual note tabs, tab naming/reordering/assignment, HUD pinning, HUD position or scale configuration, direct HUD editing, and animation polish in Canary 1; these remain approved follow-up directions after core runtime evidence.

Dependencies on Quick Stack Nearby, Inventory Search, Inventory Extended, another Workbench project, or an external service; those are cumulative compatibility targets only and are not required for standalone Notebook operation.
Changes to another project, originals, shared runtime state, either Minecraft instance, deployment, Test Slot occupancy, or any Minecraft runtime-validation claim during Canary 1 implementation.
